name: Papuan peoples of New Guinea
summary: The peoples of New Guinea, who invented farming independently around 7000 BCE at Kuk Swamp and speak hundreds of languages, more than anywhere else of similar size.

knownFor.label: Kuk Swamp
knownFor.note: Early farming site; a World Heritage Site.

knownFor.label: Taro and bananas
knownFor.note: Among the first crops grown here.

knownFor.label: Sing-sing festivals
knownFor.note: Gatherings with dance, paint and feathers.

location.value: New Guinea and neighbouring islands (Papua New Guinea and Western New Guinea), also the Torres Strait Islands and parts of Wallacea.

terrain.value: Mountain valleys, rainforest, swamps and coasts.
terrain.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

climate.value: Tropical and wet; cooler in the highlands.
climate.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

resources.value: Taro, bananas, sugar cane, sago, pigs.
resources.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

disasters.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

population.value: Unknown before contact; New Guinea’s highlands were densely farmed, and today the island has over 15 million people.
population.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

urbanisation.value: Villages and hamlets; no towns before colonial times.
urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

disease.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

migration.value: Austronesian peoples settled the coasts about 3,500 years ago.
migration.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

economicBase.value: Gardening (taro, later sweet potato), pig raising, sago.
economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

tradeRoutes.value: Trade cycles such as the kula ring and the hiri voyages.
tradeRoutes.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

wealth.value: Wealth measured in pigs and shell valuables.
wealth.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

moneyAndTax.value: Shell money, pigs and other valuables were exchanged at feasts and in bride-wealth; there were no taxes.
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

inequality.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

governmentType.value: No states; clans and villages led by “big men”.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

keyRulers.value: No rulers are recorded; leaders were “big men” who earned influence by organising feasts and exchanges.
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

succession.value: Leadership earned, not inherited, in many groups.
succession.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

institutions.value: Clan customs, exchange ceremonies such as the moka, and men’s houses where elders met.
institutions.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

stability.value: Small-scale warfare between clans was common, but the farming way of life was stable for thousands of years.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

eliteConflict.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

armyAndTech.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

majorWars.value: Frequent local clan wars over land, pigs and revenge; no large wars between states.
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

territoryChange.value: Little change for millennia; Austronesian settlers arrived on the coasts about 3,500 years ago.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

alliancesRivals.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

inventions.value: Independent invention of farming (about 7000 BCE) and drainage ditches.
inventions.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

scienceEducation.value: No writing; detailed knowledge of plants, farming and genealogy was passed on orally.
scienceEducation.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

openness.value: Highlanders were unknown to outsiders until the 1930s.
openness.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

communicationTransport.value: Walking tracks; canoes on rivers and coasts.
communicationTransport.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

religion.value: Ancestor and spirit beliefs; Christianity today.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

languageWriting.value: About 858 of New Guinea’s languages are non-Austronesian, grouped as “Papuan languages” for convenience; Indonesia lists at least 428 living ones.

artsArchitecture.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

socialStructure.value: Clans and lineages; big men gained status by generosity rather than by birth.
socialStructure.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

sharedIdentity.value: Hundreds of separate peoples and languages, with loyalty mainly to clan and valley.
sharedIdentity.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

dailyLife.value: Houses of wood and thatch, some on stilts; taro, sweet potato, sago and pork.
dailyLife.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

neighbours.value: Austronesian peoples on the coasts and islands; later Dutch, German and British colonists.
neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

colonisation.value: Colonised by the Dutch, Germans and British (1880s); Papua New Guinea independent 1975.
colonisation.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

riseSignals.value: People reached Sahul (Australia–New Guinea) between 50,000 and 37,000 years ago; a 2025 proposal suggests about 60,000 years ago.

peakPeriod.value: No single peak; sweet potato (from about 1700) allowed highland populations to grow.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

declineSignals.value: Colonial rule from the 1880s and disease, though many communities kept their land.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

outcome.value: Papuan peoples live in Papua New Guinea and Indonesia today.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp

sources.source: Wikipedia: Papuan people; Wikipedia: Kuk Swamp
